# #722 — Both pre-push done-means checks (705, 712) are RED on untouched main: unpinned fixture core.hooksPath trips #711's assertion, misreported as substantive regressions

State: OPEN
Author: rodaddy
Labels: none
Created: 2026-08-10T14:21:04Z
Updated: 2026-08-10T14:21:57Z

---

## Family classification

**Family B** — environment deciding a verdict. A cross-defect INTERACTION: the
#711 fix (an assertion added to the hook) breaks the #705 check's fixtures,
because those fixtures never isolated the environment they inherit.

## Defect

`scripts/done-means/705-pre-push-base-selection.sh` is **RED (exit 1), 5 of 6
clauses failing, on the untouched primary checkout at `183d066`** — with a
clean tree and no local modifications.

The #705 fix itself is NOT broken. The check's fixtures are.

Line 146 builds each throwaway repo with a bare init:

```sh
git -C "$FIXTURE" init -q -b main
```

which sets no `core.hooksPath`, so the fixture inherits the operator's GLOBAL
value (`/Users/rico/.config/git/hooks`). #711 later added an assertion to
`_githooks/pre-push` that refuses any `core.hooksPath` other than `_githooks`.
That assertion runs BEFORE the `--explain` early exit, so every fixture
invocation now dies at the hooksPath check and prints the #711 refusal instead
of the base-selection output the clauses parse:

```
CLAUSE a: FAIL — decision fields missing from the explain output (memory='' openbrain=''):
  ✗ core.hooksPath does not match what _githooks/install.sh writes.
      configured: /Users/rico/.config/git/hooks
      expected:   _githooks
CLAUSE c: FAIL — the hook did not name the base ref it compared against: <same refusal>
CLAUSE d: FAIL — an upstreamless branch made the hook fail rather than fall back (exit=1)
CLAUSE f: FAIL — the real push path produced no readable package decision
```

Clause b's message is actively misleading — "a real python/openbrain edit was
NOT detected", "the packages are no longer separately gated" — describing a
#705 regression that has not happened. The empty strings it reports are parse
failures against a refusal, not classification failures.

## Proof the hook is sound

Same shipped `_githooks/pre-push`, same fixture shape, with the one line the
fixture is missing (`git config core.hooksPath _githooks`):

```
$ (cd $FIXTURE && ./_githooks/pre-push --explain)
  base: main — fallback (no configured upstream, no origin/main)
  changed: python/openbrain-memory=no python/openbrain=no parity=no
  base_ref=main
  base_source=fallback (no configured upstream, no origin/main)
```

Base resolution, announcement, and package flags all behave. The defect is
entirely in the fixture's environment isolation.

## Why this matters more than a red check

A standing check that is RED for a reason unrelated to its subject, while
printing "the packages are no longer separately gated", is how a real #705
regression would get waved through as "that one's always red." It also blocks
the round-28 practice of proving pre-existing failures against the untouched
primary: this check can no longer answer whether #705 holds.

## Done-means suggestion

Fix inside this check (it is its own subject):

1. Every fixture repo sets `core.hooksPath=_githooks` (or is invoked with
   `git -c core.hooksPath=_githooks`) immediately after `git init`, so it is
   hermetic against the operator's global config. RED→GREEN is the whole proof:
   the check goes green on an unmodified `_githooks/pre-push`.
2. Add a clause that FAILS LOUDLY when the hook's output does not contain the
   `base_ref=` / `changed_*=` fields at all, reporting "the hook refused before
   reaching --explain: <first line>" rather than reporting empty decision
   fields as a classification defect. A parse failure and a wrong answer are
   different defects with different owners (round 29).
3. Guard the whole suite: assert the fixture's effective `core.hooksPath`
   equals `_githooks` before running any clause; a mismatch is HARNESS-ERROR
   (exit 3), not FAIL.

Generalisable: any done-means fixture that runs a git hook must pin
`core.hooksPath`, or #711's assertion will fire inside it.

## Discussion (1)

### rodaddy — 2026-08-10T14:21:56Z

**Scope widened after a class sweep — this is not a single-check defect.**

`scripts/done-means/712-pre-push-pipe-safe.sh` is the SECOND victim of the same
root cause, and it is worse: **6 of 6 clauses FAIL on the untouched primary at
`183d066`**, i.e. the check is entirely blinded.

`712-pre-push-pipe-safe.sh:172` has the identical bare init:

```sh
git -C "$FIXTURE" init -q -b main
```

so the fixture inherits the global `core.hooksPath` and every clause parses
#711's refusal text instead of the hook's real output:

```
CLAUSE a: FAIL — a GREEN suite through a pipe still failed the hook (exit=1): ... (issue #711)
CLAUSE b: FAIL — a genuine test failure was not reported as a test failure
CLAUSE c: FAIL — the write/runner failure was not named as one
CLAUSE d: FAIL — the redirect was silent — no announcement naming the log ... (issue #711)
CLAUSE e: FAIL — the runner's output never reached the caller ... (issue #711)
CLAUSE f: FAIL — the runner's STDERR is still attached to a pipe (exit=1)
```

Every one of those messages asserts a #712 regression. **None has occurred** —
the fix is present and intact in the shipped hook (`_githooks/pre-push`: the
`TEST_LOG` redirect of both fds, the verdict read from `TEST_EXIT`, and the
`WriteFailed` classification branch). Clause f is the most dangerous: it states
"redirecting stdout alone does not fix #712" about a hook that redirects both.

## The class

Sweep of every done-means check that builds a git fixture:

| check | pins `core.hooksPath`? | live status on untouched main |
|---|---|---|
| `711-hookspath-relative.sh` | YES | GREEN 5/5 |
| `709-hook-feeds-head-ref.sh` | YES | GREEN |
| `714-head-ref-resolves-remote.sh` | YES | GREEN |
| `705-pre-push-base-selection.sh` | **NO** | **RED, 5/6 clauses** |
| `712-pre-push-pipe-safe.sh` | **NO** | **RED, 6/6 clauses** |

The correlation is exact: pinned → green, unpinned → red. Both RED checks are
the two guarding the pre-push hook, so the gate with the most family history
currently has **no working done-means coverage at all**, while both checks
report confident, specific, wrong regression claims.

## Amended done-means suggestion

Apply the fix to BOTH checks, and add the class guard:

1. Fixtures in both `705-` and `712-` pin `core.hooksPath=_githooks` right after
   `git init`. RED→GREEN: both go green against unmodified `_githooks/pre-push`.
2. Both gain the parse-failure clause: when the hook's output lacks the expected
   fields, report "the hook refused before producing output: <first line>" —
   never a substantive regression claim derived from empty parses.
3. Shared helper, not two copies (the round-28 duplication lesson): one fixture
   constructor that pins hooksPath and asserts the effective value is
   `_githooks` before any clause runs, HARNESS-ERROR (exit 3) on mismatch.
